messages:
Ravi: Morning! Quick onboarding questions about benefits and payroll. I selected the basic medical plan during enrollment but didn't touch dental. Is dental auto-enrolled or do I need to opt in separately?
Ravi: Also, I saw an option for commuter benefits. Is that payroll pre-tax or post-tax?
Ravi: Lastly, my offer mentioned a one-time equipment stipend. Who handles the reimbursement?
people-ops-bot: Welcome to Redwood, Ravi! :tada: Helpful links: New hire checklist https://redwood.example/onboard, benefits portal https://benefits.redwood.example (SSO), payroll FAQ https://payroll.redwood.example/faq.
Maya (People Ops): Hi Ravi, congrats and great questions. Dental is not auto-enrolled; you need to opt in through the benefits portal within 30 days of your hire date to have it effective the start of the next month.
Maya (People Ops): Commuter benefits are offered as a pre-tax deduction and are set up via Workday > Benefits > Commuter. Monthly limits apply per IRS rules. If you want a combo of pre-tax transit and parking, you can elect both up to their respective caps.
Lina (Payroll): For the equipment stipend: recruiting usually flags it on your offer letter. If it's a stipend (one-time), submit an expense in Expensify with the "Equipment Stipend" tag and attach the invoice/receipt. We reimburse it on the next payroll cycle after approval. If it's an allowance added to base pay, it should be visible in Workday compensation. If you're unsure, ping Tess from recruiting.
Tess (Recruiting): Hey Ravi 020202I coordinated the stipend with hiring manager; it's a one-time stipend. I'll forward the approval note to you and to Lina so finance has the doc trail.
Ravi: Thanks all. If I miss the 30-day window for dental, can I add it later during open enrollment?
Maya (People Ops): Yes, you'll have to wait for annual open enrollment unless you have a qualifying life event. We can also fast-track enrollment if there's a special case; book a 15-min slot on our calendar and we'll help.
Ravi: Cool. On the commuter setup, does payroll take that out before or after my first paycheck? I set it up yesterday but I'm seeing full deposit tomorrow.
Lina (Payroll): Commuter deductions start after the payroll cutoff if elected after the cutoff. Since payroll runs biweekly, if you set it up after the cutoff, it will appear on the following pay. If you want me to check your setup I can confirm that your commuter election is linked to your workday profile.
Ravi: Appreciate it. One more tiny thing 020202are holidays pro-rated for new hires or do we get the full company holiday bank?
Maya (People Ops): Company observed holidays are the same for all employees and not pro-rated. Floating personal days follow the policy in the handbook and prorate for partial-year hires; see the PTO policy page: https://handbook.redwood.example/pto.
Ravi: Got it. I'll wait for Tess's note then submit the equipment receipt. Thanks everyone!
Tess (Recruiting): Sending the approval now. @Maya @Lina I included the exact stipend amount in the thread email.
Maya (People Ops): Thanks @Tess 020202I'll mark this in case we need to override anything for the first payroll.
Ravi: Thanks again :thumbsup:
